f1_story:
Paths below are under /Users/idantal/ShermanQC/FullProject.

NAMING TRAP. In the repo, "F1" is the name of a research program, and the program is named after its metric: the F1 score of bend-LINE localization.
- Matching rule: 5° angle, 4 mm transverse offset, 60% span overlap, one-to-one Hungarian assignment (scripts/evaluate_f1_against_manual_gold.py:59-64,129-175).
- Every "F1 0.xx" below is that line metric. None of them measures angle, flange length or position.
- The "engine" is a chain of versioned stages (133 backend/f1_*.py modules, ~472 F1 scripts), not one module.

ERA 0 — the runtime before F1 (Mar–Apr 2026)
- What it was: a CAD-matched progressive pipeline plus a bend-state factor model (C_i/ρ_i/A_i, two calibrated GBDT heads, Poisson-binomial count).
- Regression on 29 scans: count MAE 1.143 vs total, 0.062 vs completed, 0.882 full-scan exact (docs/BEND_REGRESSION_TESTING.md:91-105).
- These are not blind numbers. Outside blind mode the evaluator feeds expected counts and spec angles into inference (scripts/evaluate_bend_case.py:109-113), and the 10 Jul audit withdrew the "88.9%" claim.
- About 54 of ~57 count-error units came from partial scans (docs/research/MATH_SPEC_LABELS_AND_BENCHMARKS.md:166-170).

ERA 1 — zero-shot, PLY only (May to 21 Aug)
- 8 May, known-9 slice: raw exact 2/5.
- 13 Jul, bounded baseline: 0/13 exact.
- 15 Jul:
  - a "10/13 perfect" claim was withdrawn after the owner's review (1/13 under strict review);
  - schema-v5 got render-admissible count 11/13, but release-visual 0/13, P95 43 s.
- After that, Codex hand-labelled 13 scans / 71 axes.
- 16 Jul: corpus-fit 96.35% vs grouped hold-out 43.87%.
- 17 Jul, honest hold-out: 0.488 (30 TP / 22 FP / 41 FN), 0/13 exact.
- 18 Jul, Shaked-12: 0.967. But 49 of the 59 labels were snapped to existing candidates, and verified-13 stayed at 0.481.
- 29 Jul, frozen baseline: 0.264.
- 30 Jul, 12 new Gmail scans: 1/12 count-exact.
- 3 Aug, Gold-27 (37 scans / 27 parts), v21: 1.000, a development fit. On unseen parts it scored 2/9, 3/4 and 3 TP / 3 FP / 5 FN.
- 4 Aug, locked Gold37 baseline: P 0.56, R 0.231, F1 0.327, 1/37 exact.
- 5–21 Aug: versions V2 to V73, run under GPT-Pro "professor" rulings.
  - V16: 0.717, but on held-out fixtures (non-physical).
  - V51: 0.593 on 12 consumed physical scans. The candidate pool already contained 85% of the bends (recall ceiling 0.8475); 15 were lost in selection and 9 were never generated.
  - V52: 0.518.
- 20 Aug audit: "architecture-thrashing"; V74 paused.
- 30 Aug, 28 new scans: V51 scored 0.197 (P .18, R .22, 2/28 exact). A fitted 0.632 did not survive hold-out testing (0.203, 0.196, 0.104).

ERA 2 — light CAD assistance (22–27 Aug), on matched Gold11 (11 scans / 6 CAD families / 71 lines)
- Scan-only: 0.365 (0/11 exact count).
- CAD alone: 0.348 (gated) / 0.354 (pure STEP).
- Retained scan + CAD union: 0.458 (30/30/41, P .50, R .42, 1/11 exact count, 0/11 exact line sets).
- Aggressive union: 0.456.
- CAD-first localizer: 0.354 at P95 0.88 s.

ERA 3 — heavy CAD-guided rebuild (8–16 Sep)
- 8 Sep: the owner deferred zero-shot work. Targets were set at P/R/F1 ≥ 0.90 (docs/CURRENT_STATUS.md:3633-3645).
- cad_guided V1–V11 (the v18 family) on physical Gold11:
  - every completed run emitted 0 lines (V1, V2, V3, V7, V8, V9, V10: TP 0 / FP 0 / FN 71);
  - V5 aborted with no score;
  - the frozen V11 run is terminal with no F1;
  - runs took up to about 8 h.
- 14 Sep: one part scored 4/4 (STEP axes → V11 pose → raw scan support).
- 15 Sep, multi-scan topology recovery: v1 0.4286 (24/17/47; only 7/11 scans emit), v2 0.3818.
- 16 Sep, three-part diagnostic: 0.818 at 3 mm support → 0.917 at 5 mm. The CAD axes sat about 3.7 mm (max 4.728 mm) from the references. A scan-fitted line was proposed and never built.

ERA 4 — setup and CAD only (23 Sep to 1 Oct)
- Vendor setup UI: SKU, CAD, PDF, bend tags, order, מהלך groups, general measurements.
- CAD extractor V10: 120/127 known bends (94.49%), 0 false positives, complete-12 F1 98.43%.
- One random email STEP: 12/12.
- Unfold previews: 6/20 corpus parts, 3/5 fresh uploads.
- Never measured anywhere: flange length, and any incomplete (mid-sequence) scan.

RECONCILED CONTRADICTIONS
(1) "CAD gave no gain" is true for CAD alone and for the heavy rebuild. It is false for the conservative union, which gained +0.093 on matched cases. The owner's "0.518 vs 0.456" comparison used two disjoint corpora (docs/research/2026-08-27_cad_assisted_f1_deep_dive.md:9-15).
(2) The brief's "axis recovery v2 ≈ 0.43" is actually the v1 control; v2 scored 0.382.
(3) The "full V11 score 0.4286 / 0.3818" (docs/research/2026-09-16_gold11_v11_simple_family_failure_analysis.md:5-7) belongs to the topology-recovery path. The frozen V11 mesh run stayed terminal with no F1.
(4) "Gold27" and "Gold37" are the same 37 scans of 27 part IDs.
(5) The development-fit highs (0.967, 1.000, 0.632) never transferred to new parts.
current_best:
(A) COMPLETE SCANS

Bend-line localization (the only quantity F1 has ever measured)
- The best audited physical result is still the retained scan + scan-supported CAD union on matched Gold11: F1 0.458.
  - Counts: 30 TP / 30 FP / 41 FN; P 0.50, R 0.42; minimum-family recall 0.20.
  - Exact count 1/11; exact line sets 0/11.
  - This number reproduces cached bytes; it was not freshly re-run (docs/research/2026-09-10_gold11_cached_control_v2_result.md:16-30).
- Every newer attempt scores lower:
  - V11 topology recovery v1: 0.4286, and only 7 of 11 scans emit anything.
  - V11 topology recovery v2: 0.3818.
  - Scan-only V51: 0.593 on its own consumed 12-scan set, but 0.197 prospectively on 28 new scans (2/28 exact) and 0.327 on Gold37.
- The three-part 0.818 → 0.917 diagnostic covers only 12 lines.
- Nothing is near the locked ≥ 0.90 targets.

Per-bend expected vs actual (what the operator needs)
- Only the active runtime pipeline emits per-bend values: angle, radius, line-position deviations, and a tip-to-tip edge distance.
- Blind evidence: exact bend count 3/12, P95 46 s (docs/PROFESSOR_ENTERPRISE_F1_PROMOTION_CHECKPOINT_20260715.md:53-72).
- Angle MAE vs nominal on completed-part controls (docs/research/ANGLE_TRUTH_CONTROL_SET_20260404.md:33-63):

| Part(s) | Angle MAE vs nominal |
| --- | --- |
| 15651004 | 0.06° |
| 10839000 | 0.25° |
| 37361005 | 0.36° |
| 48991006, 11979003, 48963008 | 1.35–2.0° |
| 28870000 (rolled guard) | 6.4° |

- These angle figures are measured against nominal, not physical truth, and were produced by the pre-blind evaluator.
- Flange length: no engine measures it and no truth exists. Its accuracy is unknown, not low.

Verdict for (A): the runtime pipeline gives per-bend values (unqualified, stamped RESEARCH ONLY), and the CAD+scan union gives line detection (0.458). Neither is production grade.

(B) INCOMPLETE (MID-SEQUENCE) SCANS

No engine has been designed for or evaluated on them.
- The runtime has scan_state='partial' branches, but the worker never passes a state (backend/bend_analysis_worker.py:86-94,161-174).
- The count posterior is an order-free Poisson-binomial (backend/bend_unary_model.py:683-741).
  - On 15 partial scans the predicted count sat 3.6 bends from the finished-part total, for both the heuristic and the structured model.
  - The team's own spec says partial scans carry about 54 of the ~57 total count-error units (docs/research/MATH_SPEC_LABELS_AND_BENCHMARKS.md:166-170).
  - That metric conflates "not yet formed" with "missed". No per-bend partial-scan evaluation exists anywhere.
- F1 always ran blind (state=unknown) and never scored a partial scan.
- In the cad_guided chain, "partial" means partial support, not partial forming.
- The setup's completed_steps field, the tagged bend order and the מהלך groups are planning fields that no engine reads.

Best available today: none. The closest stub is the runtime pipeline plus an operator-declared stage, and nothing wires the declared stage through.

Raw material for building (B), all in /Users/idantal/ShermanQC/source-assets/02_CAD_QC_3D: staged scans of 10839000 (full + 2 partial), 23553000 (full + 2), 28870000 (full + 1), 38172000 (×2), 40500000 (×2) and 11979003 (before-bending + full). These scans have no stage labels and are development-consumed.
runtime_reality:
What the active app actually runs (paths under /Users/idantal/ShermanQC/FullProject):

1. Alignment.
- backend/bend_analysis_worker.py:153 calls build_bend_heatmap_evidence.
- That calls qc_engine.ScanQCEngine.align(auto_scale=True, tolerance=tolerance_angle) (domains/bend/services/heatmap_evidence_service.py:156-167; backend/qc_engine.py:1321-1356).
- The alignment steps are:
  1. PCA pre-alignment.
  2. Uniform auto-scale, applied whenever the bounding-box ratios agree (CV < 0.03) and are more than 5% from 1.
  3. Flip search with point-to-point ICP.
  4. Point-to-plane ICP with a Tukey loss.
  5. RANSAC 3-2-1 datum ICP.

2. Inspection.
- Worker lines 161-174 call run_progressive_bend_inspection (backend/bend_inspection_pipeline.py:3952) in blind form: spec_bend_angles_hint=None, expected_bend_override=None, use_part_truth_hints=False, and no scan_state.
- So partial-scan logic is off; _resolve_scan_state (worker 86-94) refuses to infer the state.
- The pipeline:
  - extracts CAD bend specs (:1429, :1507);
  - runs a RANSAC/dihedral BendDetector with a greedy per-CAD-bend ProgressiveBendMatcher (:3871);
  - runs CAD-local section measurement only as a fallback, for dense scans (≥ 550k points) that under-recover (:2266-2300, :4090-4102).
- That fallback lazily imports measure_all_scan_bends from the top-level backend/bend_detector.py (:3271 → :2608 → parent-frame profile sections at :2397). One reader said this file is test-only; it is not.

3. Per-bend output.
- BendMatch (backend/feature_detection/bend_detector.py:200-245) carries:
  - angle and radius deviation, and status;
  - line length, start, end and centre deviations;
  - arc length and observability states;
  - an "edge-to-edge flange distance".
- That distance is between the two boundary points farthest from the bend line, picked by arg-max (:369-405). It is the only flange-like number anywhere, and it has never been evaluated.

4. Count.
- promote_structured_count_reporting (worker :227 → domains/bend/services/structured_count_reporting_service.py:37-95) rewrites the headline completed count.
- It uses the median of a Poisson-binomial over independent per-bend probabilities (backend/bend_unary_model.py:683-741; bootstrap GBDT bundles from 2026-03-15).
- It ignores bend order.

5. Labelling. Every table is prefixed "RESEARCH ONLY - NOT QUALIFIED FOR PRODUCTION ACCEPT/REJECT" (worker :78).

6. Not called by the runtime.
- No f1_*, zero_shot_*, patch_graph_* or cad_guided_* module (including V11/v18).
- Not extractor V10.
- Not the vendor-setup draft. Its marks, sequence, machine_moves, completed_steps and general_measurements are stored in part_catalog only; rg finds no consumer outside tests.

7. Setup page.
- Uploads CAD (.stl/.ply/.obj/.step/.stp) and PDF (frontend/react/src/features/part-catalog/pages/VendorSetupPage.tsx:546-547).
- The folded/unfolded toggle (:103) is fed by unfold worker v1 by default, or v2–v4 via SHERMAN_VENDOR_UNFOLD_RUNTIME (apps/api/services/vendor_setup_service.py:211-218).
- There is no flat-pattern upload.

8. Honest evidence for this path.
- Blind CAD+PLY exact bend count: 3/12, P95 46.3 s.
- The March figures (0.882 full exact, 0.062 completed MAE) came from an evaluator that fed truth into inference (scripts/evaluate_bend_case.py:109-113).

9. Latent defects.
- Continuous auto-scale can absorb a real uniform dimensional error.
- The angle tolerance, in degrees, is reused as the datum-acceptance threshold in mm: "median < 3 × tolerance" (qc_engine.py:1820-1823; also pipeline :2357).
- PCA/bounding-box pre-alignment against the finished CAD is ill-posed for partially bent parts.
why_cad_guided_did_not_help:
Short answer: CAD did help a little in one form. Every other form gave no gain or produced nothing. And the instrument could not see what CAD is actually good at.

1. WHAT THE NUMBERS SAY
Same 11 scans and 71 lines (cached control v2:27-30; deep dive:21-24):

| Arm | F1 | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Scan-only | 0.365 | baseline |
| CAD alone (gated) | 0.348 | worse than scan-only |
| CAD alone (pure STEP) | 0.354 | worse than scan-only |
| Conservative union | 0.458 | +0.093: +11 TP for +16 FP |
| Aggressive union | 0.456 | +6 TP for +21 FP over conservative |
| CAD-first localizer | 0.354 | |
| Heavy cad_guided rebuild | 0 lines | |
| V11 recovery v1 / v2 | 0.4286 / 0.3818 | neither beats 0.458 |

- Scan-only and CAD share only 10 true positives, so the two sources are complementary.
- The owner's "0.518 vs 0.456" compared two disjoint corpora (deep dive:9-15).
- Net: CAD gave no gain as a detector, a modest recall gain as a supplement, and a large regression in the heavy rebuild.

2. CAD WAS ASKED THE WRONG QUESTION
- It was used as a candidate-line generator in a blind bend-discovery contest: state=unknown, no counts, no order (07-15 checkpoint:53-72). Line-F1 was the only score.
- What CAD actually knows was never used and never scored: which bends exist, their nominal angle, length and position, and the bend order.
- Flange length was hard-coded to None in the cad_guided chain and appears in no evaluator.

3. WRONG LOCUS (verified in source)
- Both the CAD-first template (scripts/compile_cad_bend_template_v1.py:26-33) and V11 recovery (backend/cad_guided_v11_topology_recovery_v1.py:24,97,101) project axis['line_start'/'line_end'] from scripts/extract_step_topology_bend_axes.py.
- Those points lie on the cylinder axis, i.e. the centre of curvature (:48-69). The extractor's own docstring (:84) says this is "not the bend marker on the sheet".
- The extractor's canonical mid-thickness line (:240-265) went unused.
- A centre-of-curvature line sits at least Ri (inner radius) from the inner surface and Ri + t from the outer surface. That causes two problems:
  - The 3 mm nearest-point support gate (scripts/build_additional_line_label_review.py:82-85; V11 SUPPORT_RADIUS_MM = 3.0) structurally rejects bends with larger radii. On 49001000 the axes had median distances of 2.3–4.6 mm to the scan; two were rejected and one was cut to half its span (V11 analysis:45-57).
  - Every accepted line is offset from a surface-drawn reference by roughly the radius: about 3.7 mm on accepted axes, 4.728 mm at most, against the scorer's 4.0 mm limit (V11 analysis:30-33,58-59,78-80).
- The physics was already documented (CURRENT_STATUS.md:3719-3721: the flange-plane intersection is not the cylinder axis; they are √2·R apart at 90°), but no consumer switched to the right locus.
- How much of the gap this explains is unmeasured. One re-score with the canonical or surface locus would quantify it.

4. ONTOLOGY MISMATCH
- One physical bend yields several CAD primitives: inner and outer skins, hole walls, lips, rolled or tangent transitions. Unfiltered CAD therefore adds false positives (deep dive:38-60).
- The CAD-first visual review found that registration generally places axes on the correct metal; interpretation was the main problem.
- In production this is settled once per SKU by the operator's confirmed bend tags, not once per scan.

5. REGISTRATION MISMATCH
- Fitting a partial scan to the full CAD lets self-occluded surfaces bias ICP.
- For an incomplete part, a single rigid fit to the finished CAD is mathematically impossible (docs/2026-09-23_vendor_setup_plan.md:49-54).

6. OVER-GATING KILLED THE HEAVY REBUILD
- Certificate-style gates refused real scans:
  - 0.5 mm P95 residual;
  - 0.95 support;
  - triangle-admission arithmetic;
  - more than 32 triangle-competitor caps;
  - CPU kills;
  - all 43 windows refused by the flange policy in V8.
- Runs took up to about 8 h and still emitted zero lines (CURRENT_STATUS.md:606-625, 680-712, 808-832, 1052-1128, 3241-3246).

7. THE INSTRUMENT WAS TOO SMALL AND TOO SOFT
- 11 scans, 6 families, 71 lines.
- The line convention was never signed, and the labels are AI-assisted.
- Two cases supply half of the cached true positives (CURRENT_STATUS.md:3012-3015).
- A +0.09 F1 shift on a set this fragile is hard to read either way. "No measurable gain" is as much a verdict on the instrument as on the engine.
production_engine_design:
All paths are under /Users/idantal/ShermanQC/FullProject.

PRINCIPLE: The CAD plus the operator's confirmed setup decide WHAT to inspect, once per SKU. Each scan only answers HOW FAR each planned characteristic deviates, or says UNKNOWN. Blind bend discovery leaves the critical path.

A. ONBOARDING COMPILE (once per SKU revision, offline)

1. Inputs
- STEP (required). SLDPRT deliveries must be exported to STEP.
- PDF drawing: tolerances and dimension conventions.
- NEW flat-pattern slot: DXF, TRUMPF GEO or flat STEP (optional).
- The confirmed vendor-setup draft (apps/api/services/vendor_setup_service.py:24-74): marks (feature_id, target_angle, target_radius, review_status), sequence, machine_moves (the מהלך groups), general_measurements and completed_steps.
- No engine reads this draft today. The plan compiler is the missing bridge.

2. Bend inventory
- Use extractor V10 (scripts/extract_step_topology_bend_axes_v10.py + backend/cad_finite_native_curve_graph_domain_v3.py): 120/127 known bends, 0 false positives, about 1.5 s per CAD.
- The operator corrects it during tagging, so inventory errors are fixed once rather than per scan.
- Rolled, hemmed, spline and stepped features are declared UNSUPPORTED here, before any scan.

3. Flange graph
- Planar panels joined by bends; it must be a tree.
- Root: the drawing's datum panel, or else the panel that never moves in the sequence.
- Per bend, store:
  - parent and child faces;
  - Ri (inner radius), t (thickness) and sweep;
  - the cylinder axis AND the surface loci (inner/outer apex, inner/outer virtual sharp).
- Never publish the cylinder axis as a bend line.

4. Nominals with explicit conventions
- Angle: deflection or included, per the drawing.
- Flange length per side:
  - default: from the outer mold line (OML) to the free edge;
  - when the flange ends in another bend: OML to that bend's OML;
  - tangent-to-edge: what backend/vendor_flange_preview.py:383-384 gives today.
- Bend-line position: the OML in the datum frame.
- Tolerances: per characteristic from the drawing, with no invented defaults.

5. Stage models S_0..S_P, where P = number of מהלך groups
- Method A (default):
  - For each not-yet-formed group, rotate its child subtree by −sweep about the CAD bend axis.
  - Replace the bend cylinder with a flat strip of neutral length α(Ri + K·t). Use the shop K-factor if known; otherwise flag ±α·K·t, about ±1 mm at 90° with t = 1.5.
  - This generalises _child_transform (backend/vendor_unfold_preview.py:921) and needs no full-skin unfold proof. It covers the ~94% of CADs with extracted bends, not just the 6/20 that fully unfold.
  - Overlap checks are off for intermediate stages.
- Method B (when a real shop flat is bound): fold the flat by groups 1..k.
- Precompute, per stage, a face-labelled 0.5 mm sample cloud plus a KD-tree.

6. Flat intake (the upload the owner asked for)
- An upload slot next to CAD and PDF (VendorSetupPage.tsx:546-547), plus a /flat route modelled on the drawing upload.
- An ezdxf parser for loops, the bend-line layer or linetype, and angle / UP / DOWN text.
- Binding flat bend lines to CAD feature_ids:
  - panel-tree graph match;
  - 2D rigid or mirror ICP against the CAD development, when one exists;
  - operator click-to-confirm on symmetric parts.
- The stored mapping drives the unfolded tagging view. It replaces today's rule that every mark must be a CAD candidate.
- Onboarding QA: compare the flat's developed lengths with the folded CAD under the shop K, so an inconsistent plan is flagged early.
- The current reverse-engineered flats can only test this plumbing.

B. PER-SCAN PIPELINE
Target: P95 ≤ 30 s; hard stop at 120 s → UNKNOWN(TIMEOUT); ≤ 2 GB; CPU only.

1. Ingest
- PLY in declared mm; scale fixed at 1.0.
- Disable the continuous auto-scale (qc_engine.py:1409-1444). Allow only an exact declared 25.4 or 1000 factor.
- 0.5 mm voxel cloud for registration; full-resolution KD-tree for measurement.

2. Stage hypotheses
- Only prefixes at מהלך boundaries: P+1 hypotheses, not 2^N.
- If the cell or operator declares k (completed_steps), score k and k±1; otherwise score all.

3. Registration, per hypothesis
- Coarse: a stored per-SKU fixture pose, or datum-island features (largest panel plane plus a 2D outline and hole match over the symmetric candidates).
- Fine: trimmed or Tukey point-to-plane ICP on the visible overlap only, anchored on the datum island.
- Keep the top-2 poses and their margin.
- Reuse qc_engine's Tukey ICP (:1489) and RANSAC datum step (:1512).
- Drop PCA pre-alignment for partial stages.
- Stop passing the angle tolerance as the mm datum tolerance (qc_engine.py:1820-1823).

4. Stage decision
- Posterior over k from the robust residual, coverage, and a per-bend normal-turn test (formed → dihedral near nominal; unformed → coplanar).
- Declared ≠ inferred → STAGE_MISMATCH, routed to review. Never override silently.
- Ambiguous → the bends in the ambiguous groups are UNKNOWN.

5. Section metrology, for each bend formed in stage k̂
- Segment scan points to the parent and child faces using the registered S_k̂ labels (≤ 1.5–2 mm, normals within 15–20°). Exclude the bend zone, holes and edges.
- Cut 5–11 stations along the visible bend length. In each station:
  - fit both flange lines; their normals give the angle;
  - the virtual sharp (OML, or inner surface + t when only the inside is visible) gives the bend-line position as a transverse offset plus skew;
  - a robust boundary fit of the free edge in the flange plane gives the flange length per side (OML to OML for bend-to-bend flanges);
  - radius is optional: a circle tangent to the fitted flanges.
- Aggregate by median. Report min and max to show crowning and taper.
- The uncertainty U comes from the station spread (MAD), the fit residual and a pose-perturbation test.
- Angle and flange length depend on the pose only through segmentation, so about 1 mm of registration error does not bias them. Position does depend on the pose, hence the datum anchoring.
- Build on backend/bend_detector.py:2397 and :1516. Today these run only as a fallback (bend_inspection_pipeline.py:2266-2300, 4090-4102). Extend their ±30 mm sections to the full flange.

6. Bends not yet formed (groups > k̂)
- NOT_YET_FORMED after a coplanarity check; if the bend is in fact formed → UNEXPECTED_FORMED.
- A flange length that ends on a not-yet-formed bend is NOT_APPLICABLE; its developed length is informational only.

7. The setup's general_measurements are computed from the measured lines and points.

8. Optional, offline first: a residual lane that flags creases S_k̂ does not explain, for REVIEW only.

C. UNKNOWN SEMANTICS (implements roadmap:237-248)

Status values:

| Level | Allowed values |
| --- | --- |
| Part validity | VALID, INSUFFICIENT_CAPTURE, UNTRUSTED_REGISTRATION, WRONG_PART_SUSPECTED, UNSUPPORTED_INPUT |
| Stage | CONFIRMED, MISMATCH, AMBIGUOUS |
| Bend | FORMED, NOT_YET_FORMED, UNEXPECTED_FORMED, MISSING, UNKNOWN, UNSUPPORTED |
| Characteristic | MEASURED {value, U, deviation, PASS/FAIL/REVIEW}, or UNKNOWN {OCCLUDED, EDGE_NOT_SEEN, LOW_DENSITY, AMBIGUOUS_SEGMENTATION, REGISTRATION_UNTRUSTED, TIMEOUT} |

Decision rule (guard band):
- PASS only if |dev| + U ≤ tolerance.
- FAIL only if |dev| − U > tolerance.
- Otherwise REVIEW.

Hard rules:
- UNKNOWN never becomes PASS or FAIL.
- The nominal value is never copied into "actual".
- A part is OK only when every required characteristic is MEASURED and PASS.
- Extend BendMatch (feature_detection/bend_detector.py:200-245) with per-side flange-length fields and U. Replace the arg-max tip distance (:369-405).

D. RUNTIME BUDGET (P95)

| Step | Budget |
| --- | --- |
| Load and downsample | ≤ 3 s |
| Registration (≤ P+1 hypotheses × ~1 s ICP on 30–50k points) | ≤ 8 s |
| Stage decision | ≤ 1 s |
| Metrology (≤ 0.3 s per bend × ≤ 16 bends) | ≈ 5 s |
| Report | ≤ 3 s |
| Total | ~20 s typical, ~30 s P95 |

All CAD work is precomputed at onboarding. Why this budget is realistic:
- CAD-first localization ran at P95 0.88 s after registration.
- The blind runtime is at P95 46 s.
- The owner recalls about 30 s per scan.
- The cad_guided v18 chain takes 10–20 minutes per scan.

E. REUSE VS BUILD NEW

Reuse:
- Extractor V10, plus operator confirmation.
- The vendor-setup draft and UI: folded/unfolded toggle, order, מהלך colours, PDF export.
- vendor_flange_preview (nominal flange depth).
- vendor_unfold_preview's hinge math.
- qc_engine's registration pieces.
- The bend_detector.py section measurement.
- The BendMatch schema.
- line_scan_support (scripts/build_additional_line_label_review.py:125) and _two_surface_normal_turn (scripts/apply_f1_step_topology_targeted_verifier.py:72), as fast formed/observed checks.
- runtime_semantics' ternary states.
- The Hungarian line matcher and the CAD reference scorer, as secondary checks.
- The F1 candidate pool and V16–V51, only as an offline residual detector.

Keep off the critical path:
- cad_guided V1–V11 / v18 (0 physical lines, flange None, 10–20 min per scan).
- The structured CP-SAT lane (1/37 exact).
- The train18 candidates.
- The order-free Poisson-binomial count (bend_unary_model.py:683-741).

Build new:
- The plan compiler.
- Flat intake, parser and binding.
- Stage synthesis and the stage decoder.
- Flange-length and position metrology with uncertainty U.
- The decision / UNKNOWN contract.
- The per-bend benchmark and the injected-error generator.
accuracy_roadmap: Step 0, definitions and contract (prerequisite for any number). Define a per-SKU-revision inspection-plan schema. Fix the convention for each characteristic: angle as deflection or included; flange length as OML, IML or tangent per the drawing callout; bend-line locus as the OML in the datum frame; datum as the drawing datum or the root panel. Two shop authorities sign the conventions (deep dive section 5). Transcribe tolerances from the drawings. Adopt the UNKNOWN/REVIEW output contract. Gate: plans signed for 3 representative SKUs.

Step 1, build the instrument before the engine. Write the per-bend, per-characteristic scorer keyed by CAD bend ID. Build the injected-error generator, with its scanner model calibrated on real repeat scans. Remap the 33 dangling corpus symlinks to source-assets. Run the current runtime pipeline in blind mode as the control arm to get the first honest per-bend baseline. Also run one settling diagnostic, labelled as a diagnostic: re-score the CAD-first/V11 lane on consumed Gold11 using the extractor's canonical mid-thickness line instead of the cylinder axis, with the support radius measured from the sheet surface. This quantifies how much of 'CAD did not help' came from the wrong-locus defect.

Step 2, physical truth at the shop. Pick at least 8 families that have a STEP file and parts available. Measure every bend with calipers, protractor and height gauge at 3 stations, by 2 people. Take 3 re-fixtured repeat scans per part on the Zeiss cell. Scan at least 3 parts after every מהלך. Bend at least 3 parts wrong on purpose. Ask the shop for real TruTops DXF/GEO flats for the same SKUs. Gate: the repeatability of the hand measurement itself is known, because it bounds every later accuracy claim.

Step 3, onboarding compile and flat intake. Build the plan compiler from the confirmed setup draft plus extractor V10. Add the flat upload slot, the DXF parser, flat-to-CAD bend binding with operator confirmation, and an unfolded tagging view driven by the bound flat. Generate stage models by hinge rotation. Gate: all 20 approved STEPs compile or list their UNSUPPORTED features explicitly. Binding must round-trip on the reverse-engineered flats (this tests plumbing only) and later on real shop flats.

Step 4, complete-scan metrology v1. Registration reuses the qc_engine pieces with auto-scale off, anchors on the datum island and keeps the top-2 poses. Section metrology measures angle, flange length per side, OML position and uncertainty U, with guard-band decisions. Synthetic gates: bias at most 0.05 mm / 0.1 deg, P95 at most 0.2 mm / 0.3 deg, and zero false PASS. Proposed physical gates on dev parts, to be re-based to at most 1/3 of each drawing tolerance: flange length P95 at most 0.3 mm, angle P95 at most 0.5 deg, position P95 at most 0.5 mm, at least 90% of required characteristics MEASURED, gauge R&R at most 30% of tolerance, and P95 time at most 30 s. It must beat the runtime control on every metric.

Step 5, incomplete-scan v1. Decode the stage over prefixes at מהלך boundaries, verify the declared stage, and emit NOT_YET_FORMED / UNEXPECTED states. Gates: correct stage on at least 98% of staged dev scans, with zero silent overrides. Errors on formed bends stay inside the Step 4 budget. No unformed bend is ever reported FAIL. Synthetic order swaps and missing or extra bends are detected.

Step 6, one frozen prospective test. At least 30 scans across at least 15 families, covering complete scans, staged scans and defective pairs. Truth is measured before the engine runs. Run it once, with every case in the denominators. Report per-characteristic error with family-cluster bootstrap confidence intervals, coverage, false-accept rate at a fixed review rate, and the worst family. Passing this test gates floor use.

Step 7, shadow mode on the floor. Run on every scanned part alongside the operator's manual checks. Track the operator review save rate at a fixed false-accept ceiling, and track drift per SKU. Go live family by family when the gates hold. Every new SKU enters through the onboarding compile.

Step 8, optional lanes, only after Step 6 and only on the same instrument: the Jev judgment, the F1 residual detector, radius metrology and learned observability. Retire the V16-V51 and cad_guided chains from the product path. Drop the per-iteration PRE/POST custody process in development and keep it for the frozen test only.
benchmark_design:
PRINCIPLE: Build the measuring instrument first. Score per characteristic and per CAD bend ID, not per free 3D line. Paths are under /Users/idantal/ShermanQC/FullProject.

1. SCORER

For every (scan, plan bend ID, characteristic), record: truth, engine value, U, state and decision.

Report:
- Error: bias, MAE and P95 |error| for flange length per side (mm), angle (°) and bend-line position (mm). Radius is optional.
- Coverage: the share of characteristics that are MEASURED.
- Decision quality: false-accept rate on out-of-tolerance characteristics, and false-reject rate at a fixed review rate (the professor's operator-review-save metric).
- Stage: stage accuracy and out-of-order detection.
- Repeatability: gauge R&R as a percentage of tolerance.
- Worst family.
- Runtime: P50 and P95 latency, and memory (RSS).

Rules:
- UNKNOWN counts as abstention, never as correct.
- Failures and timeouts stay in the denominators.
- Confidence intervals come from a family-cluster bootstrap.
- The 5°/4 mm line matcher stays, but only as a localization diagnostic.
- Every arm runs on the same cases and truth (deep dive:182-187).
- The current blind runtime pipeline is the control arm.

2. SPLITS

DEV (consumed: iterate freely, never quote as accuracy):
- About 84 PLY in data/bend_corpus/incoming:
  - Shaked count-backed: 12;
  - V/X good/defective pairs, e.g. 38172000, 38965002, 47251002, 50545000, 50546000, 35705010, 38173000, 50556000, 50757000;
  - 28 daily scans;
  - opaque U01–U04.
- 30 PLY and 23 STEP over 22 part IDs in /Users/idantal/ShermanQC/source-assets/02_CAD_QC_3D, including the staged sets.
- Gold11 and physical15.
- Eyal 50 is STL/SLDPRT, not scans, so it serves the CAD side only.
- Prerequisite: all 33 scan symlinks in data/bend_corpus/parts/*/scans point to the missing /Users/idant/Downloads and must be remapped.

FROZEN TEST (prospective, one shot):
- New scans from the production Zeiss cell, captured after the engine and config hashes are frozen.
- At least 30 scans across at least 15 families. Each family gets a complete scan plus a scan after every מהלך; the stage labels come free from the tagged order.
- At least 5 good/defective pairs.
- Opaque SHA-256 IDs, an evaluator-only manifest, and truth measured before the engine runs.
- N001–N014 (opaque) and EHO4 (email, unopened) are the only existing material that might qualify; confirm their custody status first.
- Email parts nobody has opened are the cheapest new CAD-side material. Physical truth still needs the actual parts.

3. SYNTHETIC INJECTED-ERROR SUITE (qualifies the math; never quoted as physical accuracy)

Source: the 20 approved STEPs plus email STEPs, each with its confirmed bend order, giving S_k for every prefix.

Injected errors:
- angle: ±0.25 / 0.5 / 1 / 2 / 5°;
- flange length: ±0.1 / 0.2 / 0.5 / 1 / 2 mm;
- bend-line shift: ±0.5 / 1 / 2 mm;
- radius: ±0.5 mm;
- per-group springback;
- swapped group order;
- missing or extra bend;
- mirrored part;
- wrong SKU.

Virtual scanner:
- the cell's robot viewpoints, so self-occlusion is realistic;
- noise, outliers, edge flare, dropout and density calibrated to real repeat Zeiss scans (idealised sensors flatter accuracy);
- a random part pose.

Gates:
- bias ≤ 0.05 mm / 0.1°;
- P95 ≤ 0.2 mm / 0.3° at full visibility;
- zero false PASS;
- exact stage decoding where unambiguous, and AMBIGUOUS (never a wrong stage) on symmetric parts;
- more occlusion must raise UNKNOWN, not errors.

4. PHYSICAL TRUTH NEEDED (none exists today)

- Flange length per side at 3 stations, with calipers or a height gauge in the drawing's convention.
- Angle at 2–3 stations, with a digital protractor.
- Bend-line position against a datum hole or edge, with a height gauge or CMM.
- Thickness.
- Two people measuring, to know the hand-measurement R&R.
- 3 re-fixtured repeat scans per part. These need no truth at all.
- Deliberately mis-bent scrap parts, for example +2° or the backgauge set +1 mm.
- A ZEISS INSPECT report on the same scans, as an independent-algorithm reference.
- Real TruTops flats. The current reverse-engineered flats only test plumbing.

5. UNTIL TRUTH EXISTS

Report only repeatability, nominal-relative results on known-good parts (labelled as bounded by process variation) and the synthetic gates.
jev_hook:
WHAT JEV IS (from the TypeSafe docs saved in the session scratchpad)
- TypeSafe's "System One" model. It reads text only: strings, JSON or arrays. No images, no point clouds.
- It returns calibrated typed answers: Noul = P(yes), Choice and Score.
- Versions: jev-latest = jev-1.13.0; jev-preview = jev-1.14.0 (released 2026-10-14).
- Context: 64k tokens per request, 32k per question. Price: $0.042 per million input tokens.
- One set of weights serves every customer, so domain knowledge enters only through the state and the instructions/criteria.
- Its own docs recommend feeding its probabilities into a classical model downstream.
- It is not referenced anywhere in the repo today.

WHERE IT FITS IN THE F1 CANDIDATE FLOW (scripts/build_f1_retained_stage_graph_v1.py:21-30)

The current flow:
1. PLY → candidate pool (scripts/build_f1_scan_only_candidate_pool.py). That is about 480 line candidates per scan; 5,787 over physical15.
2. Per-candidate descriptors (research/f1_multifamily_selector_v2/model.py:31-94): span, radius, support fractions, two-sided normal angle and balance, normal spreads, neighbour counts, source.
3. V16 selector (scripts/select_f1_mesh_route_v16.py:67-86): two GBDT heads.
4. Then V43 two-sided support, V44 stitch, V50 ownership, V47, V48/V49 NMS, and finally V51.

Insert Jev between step 2 (descriptor construction) and step 3 (V16):
- Option 1: add jev_p_bend as an extra GBDT column. The v9/v4 bundles must be retrained.
- Option 2, no retraining: ask Jev only about candidates whose V16 score is in an uncertainty band, before the V43–V51 stages. Selection and ownership is where recall is lost: the pool's recall ceiling is 0.8475, but only 0.593 is selected (15 bends lost in selection, 9 never generated).

The question to ask:
- A Noul: "Is this a press-brake bend line?"
- State: the descriptors as named fields with units, a neighbour summary, scan context, and in the CAD lane the nearest planned bend (ID, offset, angle).
- Criteria: the documented confusers — perimeter/outline, hole wall, rolled band, step, inner/outer duplicate skin, the 4.8 mm tongue silhouette (evaluate_f1_against_manual_gold.py:6-7), and scan artifacts.

The same Noul can gate CAD additions before the union step (apply_f1_cad_guided_scan_frame_gate.py → diagnose_f1_cad_scan_fusion_gold11.py). The union bought +11 TP for +16 FP, so a precision gate there is useful. Fix the cylinder-axis locus defect first.

Limits:
- Jev cannot recover the 9 bends that were never generated.
- The GBDT already sees the same numbers, so any gain has to come from the encoded domain rules.

Measure it before claiming anything:
1. Label pool candidates with the existing 5°/4 mm/0.6 matcher on physical15 and Gold11.
2. Hold out one family at a time.
3. Compare GBDT against GBDT + Jev with a family-cluster bootstrap.
4. Confirm once on prospective scans.

IN THE PRODUCTION ENGINE

The bend list is known from the confirmed setup, so "is this a bend?" shrinks to three advisory hooks:
1. Onboarding: pre-fill the BendMark review (issue = not_a_bend / missing; vendor_setup_service.py:24-37). The operator still confirms every mark.
2. Per scan, unexplained creases: judge creases that the stage model S_k̂ does not explain (extra or out-of-order bend, or an artifact) and route them to REVIEW.
3. Per scan, borderline formed/unformed evidence: route to REVIEW.

Jev stays off the measurement path. It never sets MEASURED or PASS, never replaces UNKNOWN and never moves a value.

Operations:
- Pin a versioned model ID, not the alias.
- Send one fan-out request per scan.
- Keep a GBDT-only fallback for offline cells.
- Send descriptors only, never CAD or scan geometry.
- Log p and the model ID for every answer.
risks: Truth gap: there is no flange-length truth and no physical angle or position truth. Until Step 2 is done, every metrology number is either synthetic or measured against nominal.

Small, consumed evidence: every local physical scan is development-consumed. Gold11 is 11 scans in 6 families, and two cases supply half of the cached true positives. Development-fit highs (0.967, 1.000, 0.632) collapsed on unseen parts (2/9, 3/4, 0.197).
Soft labels: the Gold lines and the 127-bend CAD reference are largely AI-made, and the line convention was never signed. That is what produces metric artifacts such as the 3-5 mm axis offset.

Scanner domain shift: the corpus scanner, units and pose are unverified (mesh PLYs with more than 200k rows; CURRENT_STATUS.md:3451). The production Zeiss cell's output must be characterised before any synthetic calibration or threshold means anything.
Symmetry: a flat sheet with one bend can register in several poses, which assigns the wrong bend IDs. The engine needs datum features, top-2 pose margins and an AMBIGUOUS state.

Flange length is decided at the sheet edge: edge flare, burrs, dropout at grazing angles and seeing only one side of the sheet bias it by up to the thickness t. Flanges shorter than about 8-10 mm will often come back UNKNOWN.

Bending physics: springback, crowning, non-planar flanges and K-factor stretch all matter. Without a shop K-factor, an unformed strip in a stage model carries about +/-1 mm of uncertainty at 90 degrees with t = 1.5.

Flat files: the current flats were reverse-engineered from the folded CAD, so they are circular and cannot validate anything. Real DXF/GEO files vary in layers, units, mirroring and bend-line conventions.

Unsupported geometry must be declared up front: rolled (47479000), hybrid (28870000), spline (49001000), stepped boss (42288005), and closed-loop or hemmed parts. Full unfold currently works on only 6 of 20 parts.
Input formats: the newest deliveries are SLDPRT-only (the 30 Sep email, Eyal 50, the 17-20 Aug drop). Onboarding has to require a STEP export.

Runtime defects to fix before any output is trusted: auto-scale; degrees passed as a mm tolerance; the arg-max 'flange distance'; the RESEARCH ONLY stamp; all 33 corpus symlinks dangling; docs still pointing at /Users/idant.
Wrong declared stage: the operator or cell may declare the wrong completed_steps, or bend out of order. The engine must flag STAGE_MISMATCH rather than trust the declaration or override it silently.
Guard-band load: until the uncertainty U is small, many characteristics will land in REVIEW. Ambiguous drawing callouts will block automatic decisions.

Process risk in both directions: 70+ versions with multi-hour frozen runs starved iteration, while unguarded tuning produced development-fit claims. Use a fast single-scan development loop plus exactly one heavy frozen test.

Integration: the branch codex/enterprise-reorder has about 2000 uncommitted changes plus large untracked F1 trees. The new engine needs a clean module boundary, its own tests and a pinned config hash.
Jev: text-only, an external network dependency, unproven on numeric geometry descriptors, and subject to alias drift and customer-data rules. Keep it off the measurement path.
